subject.title: WhatsApp inbound messages not received in k3s nested container (outbound works)

question: Should this broad WhatsApp external-inbound-loss tracker remain canonical while maintainers choose a combined recovery design across active liveness probing, bounded backfill, and unrecoverable-gap diagnostics?
rationale: Current main partially handles delivered append events, but the remaining no-upsert symptom spans live WhatsApp behavior, privacy/read-receipt semantics, and public plugin recovery policy that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Keep Broad Tracker Canonical
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate the full no-external-upsert failure and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50093 plus https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93406 as narrower implementation slices.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Trackers
options.body: Close or demote this broad tracker only after explicitly deciding that backfill and active-liveness issues cover all remaining user-visible behavior.

options.title: Declare Current Scope Sufficient
options.body: Accept the current bounded append catch-up behavior and document container/zombie no-upsert cases as unsupported or external network/provider failures.

recommendation.title: Keep Broad Tracker Canonical
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate the full no-external-upsert failure and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50093 plus https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93406 as narrower implementation slices.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is already connected to durable inbound ownership and provider-side gap discussion, making them the best available routing owner for the recovery-policy decision.
